extracted.intended_audience: legislators, IP lawyers, collective rights management organizations, rightholders, and policymakers
extracted.subtask_description: Statutory / treaty standards governing copyright and related (neighbouring) rights, collective management, exceptions, infringement, remedies, and unfair competition for works, performances, phonograms, audiovisual fixations and broadcasts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publisher obligations to author (accounting and evidence)
rubrics_metrics.description: furnish the author with all evidence required to establish the accuracy of his accounts, failing which he may be obliged to do so by the competent domestic court.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publisher must provide accounting evidence on request; domestic courts can compel production.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publisher contractual duties on manufacture, exploitation, and attribution
rubrics_metrics.description: (i) effect or caused to be effected the manufacture in the conditions, form and mode of expression provided for in the contract; (ii) ensure that the work is continuously exploited and monitored and distributed for sale in accordance with the professional custom; (iii) Make no changes to the work without the written authorization of the author; and (iv) Unless otherwise agreed, cause to be displayed on each of the copies the name, pseudonym or mark of the author.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Four mandatory publisher duties: manufacture per contract, continuous exploitation/distribution per custom, no changes without written author authorization, and display author credit unless agreed otherwise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Representation contract
rubrics_metrics.description: A representation contract is one by which the author of a work or his successors in title authorize a legal or natural person to represent the work in conditions that he shall determine.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authorization scope is defined by the author (conditions determined by author).

rubrics_metrics.name: General representation contract by collective management organisation
rubrics_metrics.description: A general representation contract is the agreement by which the collective management organization vests a natural or legal person with the power to represent the current or future works constituting the repertoire of the organization, the author or his successors in title for the duration of the contract.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Collective management org may vest representation power over repertoire for contract duration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obligations of entertainment promoters
rubrics_metrics.description: (1) inform the author or his agents of the exact program of public performances and to furnish them with a certified statement of his takings; (2) effect the public performance under technical conditions suitable to ensure the intellectual and moral rights of the author; (3) may not transfer the enjoyment of the contract without the consent of the author.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Promoters must notify authors of programs and takings, provide suitable technical conditions protecting rights, and obtain consent before transferring contractual enjoyment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Audiovisual production contract and assignment of exclusive rights
rubrics_metrics.description: (2) Unless otherwise provided, the contract between the producer of an audiovisual work and the joint authors of such work ... shall entail the assignment of the exclusive rights in the work to the producer. However, the joint authors shall retain their graphical and theatrical rights and their right to exploit their contributions separately, unless otherwise agreed and provided that such exploitation is not likely to compete with the exploitation of the whole work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Default rule: producer receives exclusive rights; joint authors retain certain separate exploitation rights unless contractually varied and provided no competition arises.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remuneration for audiovisual authorship and mode-of-exploitation principle
rubrics_metrics.description: Remuneration as authors shall be due for each mode of exploitation. ... where the public pays a price to receive communication of a specific and individually identifiable work, the remuneration shall be proportionate to the price, having regard to any volume discounts granted by the distributor to the exploiter. It is paid to authors by the producer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors receive remuneration per exploitation mode; when public pays per-work price, remuneration should be proportionate to that price.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obligations of joint authors and the producer of the audiovisual work
rubrics_metrics.description: (1) The joint authors shall guarantee to the producer the peaceful exercise of the assigned rights. (2)(i) The producer shall ensure that the audiovisual work is exploited in accordance with the professional custom; and (ii) provide the joint authors with a statement of income ... at least once a year. At their request, he shall provide all proof of the accuracy of the accounts, in particular the copy of contracts by which he has assigned all or some of the rights at his disposal to third parties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Joint authors must secure producer's peaceful enjoyment; producer must exploit per custom and provide annual income statements and account proofs on request.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definitions: performers, fixation, phonogram, producers, audiovisual fixation
rubrics_metrics.description: Defines key terms: 'Performers' (actors, singers, musicians, dancers and other persons who perform...), 'Fixation' (incorporation of sounds/images in a material medium permanent or sufficiently stable...), 'Phonogram' (exclusively sound fixation), 'Phonogram producer' (first to take initiative/responsibility for fixing sounds), 'Audiovisual or videogram fixation' (animated sequence of images with/without sounds in a medium permitting perception), 'Audiovisual fixation producer' (natural or legal person who first fixes the images...).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These definitions set the scope and actors entitled to rights under the Part; they apply mutatis mutandis to related definitions in Part I.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of the law (territoriality and nationality rules)
rubrics_metrics.description: The provisions of this part shall apply to performances where: the performer is a national of one of the Member States; the performance takes place in the territory of a Member State; and a performance not fixed on a phonogram is incorporated into a broadcast program protected under this part. To phonograms or audiovisual fixations where the producer is a national or the first fixation was done in a Member State; to broadcast programs where the headquarters is located in a Member State or the program was transmitted from a station in a Member State.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enumerates nationality/territory-based connecting factors that trigger application of the Part's provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coexistence of copyright and related rights
rubrics_metrics.description: Related rights do not infringe copyright. Accordingly, no provision in Part II of this Annex shall be construed to limit the exercise of copyright by owners of the right.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Related/neighboring rights are independent and should not be interpreted to limit copyright exercise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Economic rights of performers (exclusive acts)
rubrics_metrics.description: Subject to Articles 62 and 63, a performer shall have the exclusive right to perform or authorize: (i) the broadcasting of his performance (with exceptions); (ii) the communication to the public of his performance (with exceptions); (iii) the fixation of his non-fixed performance; (iv) the reproduction of a fixation of his performance; (v) the distribution of copies of the fixation of his performance by sale or any transfer of ownership or by rental; and (vi) the making available to the public of his performance, such that individuals can access it at a time and place of their choosing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Performer economic rights cover broadcast, communication, fixation, reproduction, distribution, and making-available; authorizations do not generally entail other rights unless agreed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitations on authorizations (performer rights)
rubrics_metrics.description: Unless otherwise agreed: (i) the broadcasting authorization shall not entail authorization to permit other broadcasting organizations to transmit the performance; (ii) the authorization to broadcast and fix the performance shall not entail authorization to reproduce the fixation; and (iii) the authorization to fix the performance and to reproduce the fixation shall not entail authorization to broadcast the performance by means of its reproductions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authorizations are narrow by default — one specific right does not automatically include related exploitations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Moral rights of performers
rubrics_metrics.description: Independently of his economic rights and even after assignment ... the performer shall have the right to require to be mentioned as such and to oppose any distortion, mutilation or other modification of his performances ... The moral right of the performer shall attach to his person. It shall in particular be perpetual, inalienable, not subject to a limitation of time and indefeasible. It shall be transferable mortis causa.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Performer moral rights (attribution and integrity) are personal, perpetual, inalienable during life, indefeasible, but transferable on death.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rights of phonogram producers
rubrics_metrics.description: Subject to Articles 62 and 63, a producer of phonograms shall have the exclusive right to undertake or authorize: (i) the direct or indirect reproduction of his phonogram; (ii) the importation of copies of his phonogram with a view to distributing them to the public; (iii) the distribution to the public of copies of his phonogram by sale or any other means of transfer of ownership or by rental; and (iv) the making available to the public of his phonogram by wire or wireless means, such that individuals can access it at a time and place of their choosing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Producer rights mirror reproduction, importation, distribution and making-available for phonograms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rights of producers of audiovisual fixations or videograms
rubrics_metrics.description: Subject to Articles 62 and 63, a producer of audiovisual fixations or videograms shall have the exclusive right to undertake or authorize: (i) the direct or indirect reproduction; (ii) the importation of copies with a view to distribution; (iii) the distribution to the public by rental, sale, or any other means; and (iv) the making available to the public through sale, exchange, lending or communication including by wire or wireless means, such that individuals can access it at a time and place of their choosing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Producer of audiovisual fixations has comprehensive exploitation rights; these rights and certain related rights may not be separately assigned.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form of authorization (written record requirement)
rubrics_metrics.description: The authorizations referred to in this part shall, on pain of invalidity, be issued by any means that leaves a written record, including electronic media, in accordance with domestic legislation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authorizations must leave a written/electronic record to be valid.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rights of broadcasting organizations
rubrics_metrics.description: Subject to Articles 62 and 63, a broadcasting organization shall have the right to undertake or authorize: (i) retransmission of its broadcast programs; (ii) fixation of its broadcast programs; (iii) reproduction of a fixation of its broadcast programs; (iv) communication to the public of its television programs; (v) the making available to the public of its program, such that individuals can access it at a time and place of their choosing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Broadcasting organizations are granted rights to retransmit, fixate, reproduce, communicate and make-available their programs subject to exceptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equitable remuneration for broadcasting/communication of phonograms (50/50 split)
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a phonogram published for commercial purposes, or a reproduction of such phonogram, is used directly for broadcasting or communication to the public, an equitable single remuneration, intended both for the performers and the producer, shall be paid ... which shall distribute such remuneration according to the following formula: 50 per cent to performers; and 50 per cent to the producer of the phonogram.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Statutory equitable remuneration applies when phonograms are used in broadcasts/communications; collective management org distributes 50/50 between performers and producers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Implementation of equitable remuneration (scheme, consultation, arbitration)
rubrics_metrics.description: (1) The scheme and the arrangements for the receipt of the remuneration ... shall be fixed by the collective management organization in consultation with the persons using phonograms ... In the absence of agreement, an arbitration committee ... shall make a final ruling. (2) Persons using phonograms for commercial purposes shall be required to provide the collective management organization with the exact program of the use for such phonograms and all documentation indispensable for the distribution of rights.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Collective management organizations set procedures in consultation; unresolved disputes go to arbitration; users must provide exact usage programs and documentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Free use exceptions (general provisions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Notwithstanding Articles 54 to 59, beneficiaries of related rights may not prohibit: (i) private performances free of charge within a family circle; (ii) reproductions strictly for private use of the person who makes them and not intended for collective use; (iii) subject to source identification: analyses and short quotations justified by critical/argumentative/pedagogical/scientific/informational nature; press reviews; broadcasting of speeches for news etc.; (iv) communication to the public or reproduction of excerpts for educational/illustrative purposes in teaching and research; (iv) parody, pastiche and caricature; (v) provisional reproduction that is transitory or ancillary as essential/integral part of technological process enabling lawful use; (vi) reproduction and communication to the public subject to Articles 60 and 61; (vii) acts for preservation by libraries/museums/archives; and (viii) all other uses constituting exceptions regarding works protected by copyright under this Annex.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enumerates a broad set of exceptions (private use, quotation, news, educational use, parody, transient tech copies, preservation).

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement on exceptions not to impair normal exploitation or prejudice legitimate rights
rubrics_metrics.description: The exceptions set forth in this article may not impair the normal exploitation of the performance, phonogram, videogram or program or be unjustly prejudicial to the legitimate rights of the performer, producer or broadcasting organization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exceptions are subject to a three-step-like constraint: must not impair normal exploitation or cause unjust prejudice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Free use by broadcasting entities (conditions and destruction requirement)
rubrics_metrics.description: Authorizations required under Articles 54 to 59 ... shall not be required where the fixation or reproduction is effected by a broadcasting organization by its own means and for its own transmission, provided that: (i) for each transmission ... the broadcasting organization shall have the right to broadcast the performance in question; (ii) for each transmission of a fixation ... the broadcasting organization shall have the right to broadcast the transmission; and (iii) fixations and reproductions are destroyed within a time limit equivalent to that applicable to fixations and reproductions of works protected by Article 18, except for a single copy retained for preservation of archives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Broadcasting organizations may make and use their own fixations for transmission without authorizations if they have broadcast rights and destroy copies within statutory time limits, with a single archival copy allowed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Term of protection for performances
rubrics_metrics.description: (1) The term of protection for performances shall be twenty years with effect from: (i) the end of the year of fixation, for performances fixed on phonograms; and (ii) the year in which the performance took place, for performances that are not fixed. (2) Where the performance has been fixed on an audiovisual or videogram fixation, the term of protection shall be 50 years with effect from the end of the year of fixation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Different terms apply depending on fixation and medium: 20 years for most performances, 50 years where fixed on audiovisual/videogram.

rubrics_metrics.name: Term of protection for phonograms and audiovisual/videogram fixations
rubrics_metrics.description: The term of protection for phonograms and audiovisual or videogram fixations under this part shall be 50 years with effect from the end of the year of fixation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Phonograms and audiovisual fixations enjoy 50-year protection from end of fixation year.

rubrics_metrics.name: Term of protection for broadcast transmissions
rubrics_metrics.description: The term of protection for broadcast transmissions under this part of the Annex shall be 25 years with effect from the end of the year in which the transmission occurred.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Broadcast transmissions are protected for 25 years from end of transmission year.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remuneration for private copying (entitlement and levies)
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors and performers as well as producers of such phonograms and audiovisual recordings or videograms shall be entitled to remuneration referred to as compensation for private copying intended for strictly personal and private use. The remuneration shall be paid by the manufacturer or the importer of recording media or devices used for private copying ... Domestic laws shall determine the types of media or devices, the remuneration rates and the terms of payment, distribution and possible reimbursement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Private copying levies apply on manufacturers/importers; domestic law sets rates/types and reimbursement/waiver conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reimbursement/waiver of private copying remuneration for professional or assistive purchases
rubrics_metrics.description: Remuneration for private copying shall be reimbursed or waived where the recording medium or storage device is purchased in a professional capacity for private use or production by: (i) broadcasting organizations; (ii) producers of phonograms or audiovisual or videogram fixations and persons who copy such material on their behalf; (iii) legal persons or organizations which use recording or storage media to assist persons with hearing disabilities or any person who is visually impaired or has reading difficulties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific purchasers (broadcasters, producers, assistive organizations) may obtain reimbursement or waiver.

rubrics_metrics.name: Paying public domain (obligation to pay royalties for exploiting public-domain works)
rubrics_metrics.description: The exploitation of works or objects of related rights that have fallen into the public domain ... shall be subject to an undertaking by the exploiter to pay the relevant royalties to the national collective rights management organization. The royalties ... shall be equivalent to one half of the rate of remuneration normally paid to authors and holders of neighboring rights ... The revenue generated ... shall be devoted to social and cultural purposes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exploitation of public-domain works may still trigger payment of reduced royalties (half the normal rate) paid to collective management org and used for social/cultural purposes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collective management entrustment and remit
rubrics_metrics.description: The protection, exploitation and management of the rights of authors of works and the rights of holders of related rights ... shall be entrusted to one or more national collective rights management organizations, pursuant to domestic laws. The national collective rights management organization shall administer the interests of the other national and foreign bodies in national territory in accordance with conventions or agreements into which it enters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Collective management orgs are statutory administrators for rights management and international representation subject to domestic law and agreements; authors retain the right to assert their rights independently.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acts constituting counterfeiting (infringing acts)
rubrics_metrics.description: The following acts shall constitute counterfeiting: (1) any publishing, reproduction, performance, public performance or broadcast by any means whatsoever, of an object protected under this Annex; (2) the export, import and distribution of a protected object on national territory for commercial purposes in violation of the provisions of this Annex; (3) any fixation, reproduction or communication made available to the public ... in violation of the rights protected under this Annex; and (4) the marketing of graphical and three-dimensional works in violation of the right to resale royalties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Wide set of acts qualify as counterfeiting; includes distribution, reproduction, broadcasts and resale-rights violations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acts subsumed under counterfeiting (anti-circumvention and related acts)
rubrics_metrics.description: The following acts shall be subsumed under counterfeiting: (1) manufacture or import, for sale or rental, of a device or facility specifically designed or adapted to render inoperable any device designed to prevent or restrict reproduction; (2) fraudulent circumvention of effective technological measures; (3) manufacture/import of device to permit reception of encrypted program by unauthorized persons; (4) unauthorized removal or alteration of any electronic rights management information; (5) distribution or import for distribution of works in the knowledge that electronic rights management information has been removed or altered; (6) permitting reproduction or communication to the public in an establishment without first seeking prior authorization from the national collective rights management organization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Anti-circumvention, DRM removal, dealing in circumvention devices, and facilitating unauthorized reception/distribution are treated as counterfeiting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rights management information definition
rubrics_metrics.description: ‘Rights management information’ refers to information that identifies the author, work, performer, performance, phonogram producer, phonogram, producer of the audiovisual recording or videogram, audiovisual recording or videogram, broadcasting organization, broadcast and any rightholder ... or any information relating to the terms and conditions of use of the work ... when attached to the copy of a work ... or appears in connection with broadcasting, communicating or making available to the public ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines the scope of metadata/EMI protected from unauthorized removal or alteration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criminal penalties for counterfeiting
rubrics_metrics.description: Counterfeiting and subsumed acts shall be punishable by imprisonment of three months to two years and a fine of 1,000,000 to 10,000,000 CFA francs or one of those penalties alone, without prejudice to compensation for the damage suffered by the victims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sets baseline criminal sanction ranges and allows civil compensation in addition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Doubling of penalties (aggravating circumstances)
rubrics_metrics.description: The applicable penalties shall be doubled: (a) where the accused is convicted of a further act constituting infringement less than five years after having been sentenced for an earlier infringement; (b) where it is established that he habitually engages in such acts; (c) if he is the co-contracting party of the holder of the infringed right; and (d) where the infringements are committed by an organized gang.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List of aggravating factors that trigger doubled penalties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Additional criminal penalties (confiscation, destruction, closure, publication)
rubrics_metrics.description: The competent domestic court may also: (a) order confiscation of the seized revenue to the benefit of the holder of the infringed rights; (b) order confiscation and destruction of counterfeit works and of the equipment used to commit the offense; (c) order the provisional or definitive closure of the establishment in which the infringement was committed; and (d) order publication of the sentence at the expense of the convicted person.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Courts may impose additional measures beyond imprisonment/fines to remedy infringement and deter future acts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Civil penalties and determination of damages
rubrics_metrics.description: Rightholders ... shall be entitled to obtain payment by the infringer of damages as compensation for the prejudice they have suffered ... The amount of the damages shall be determined in accordance with the relevant provisions of the national civil code, taking into account the gravity of the material and moral prejudice suffered by the rightholder and the amount profit that the infringer derived from the infringement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Civil damages consider gravity of prejudice and infringer's profit; may be imposed by criminal court hearing the case.

rubrics_metrics.name: Joint liability for resale royalties violations
rubrics_metrics.description: In the event of violation of the provisions governing resale royalties, the buyer, the seller and the person tasked with the public auction may be jointly sentenced to payment of damages to beneficiaries of the resale royalties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Multiple parties in a resale chain can be held jointly liable for resale-rights breaches.

rubrics_metrics.name: Persons with locus standi (who may bring proceedings)
rubrics_metrics.description: The following persons in particular shall have locus standi: (a) holders of infringed rights or their successors in title; (b) the national collective rights management organization; and (c) professional associations of rightholders regularly constituted to defend the collective interests of their members.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lists who may institute proceedings for infringements (individual rightholders, collective organizations, professional associations).

rubrics_metrics.name: Sworn officers of collective rights management organizations
rubrics_metrics.description: The domestic law of a Member State may authorize collective rights management organizations to appoint sworn agents empowered to monitor implementation of the requirements of this Annex on national territory and ascertain offenses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Domestic law may confer investigation/monitoring powers on sworn agents of collective management orgs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obligation of public authorities to assist rightholders
rubrics_metrics.description: At the request of rightholders or their agents, bailiffs and collective management organizations, the authorities of the national police force, customs and the national gendarmerie, are required to lend their assistance and, if necessary, protection, during implementation of this Annex.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Police, customs and gendarmerie must assist rightholders enforcing rights on request.

rubrics_metrics.name: Seizure procedures for counterfeiting
rubrics_metrics.description: (1) Natural or legal persons ... may, with the approval of the Prosecutor of the Republic or the competent judge, require a judicial police officer, bailiff or any other public officer ... to ascertain the offenses and, if necessary, seize infringing copies, illegally imported copies and objects and the equipment used or to be used for performance or reproduction ... (2) The presiding judge ... may, by order made on simple request, decide to: (i) suspend any ongoing manufacturing process for the unlawful reproduction ... (ii) suspend illicit public performances; (iii) suspend any release that infringes a protected right; (iv) seize unlawfully reproduced copies ...; (v) seize the earnings generated from exploitation that infringes copyrights and neighboring rights. (3) The suspension ... may be accompanied by a fine decreed by the competent domestic court.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judicially authorized seizure and summary measures (suspensions, seizures of goods and earnings) are available to enforce rights; prosecutor/judge approval required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remedies against seizure (distrainee rights and guarantees)
rubrics_metrics.description: (1) Within 10 days of the report of the seizure, the distrainee or garnishee may request the presiding judge ... to limit its effects, or to allow the resumption of manufacture or performance, under the authority of a third-party manager to whom shall accrue the proceeds ... (2) If the request ... is granted ... the presiding judge ... may order the requester to deposit a certain amount as guarantee for the damages which the author may claim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Seized parties have 10 days to seek relief or resumption under safeguards; courts may require guarantees to protect rightholders' interests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Referral to court after seizure (15-day rule)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the party making the seizure fails to refer the matter to the competent domestic court within 15 (fifteen) days of seizure, release of the seized item(s) may be ordered ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Claimants must promptly (within 15 days) bring seized matters to court or risk release of seized items.

rubrics_metrics.name: Border measures — customs detention and procedural timeline
rubrics_metrics.description: (1) The customs department may, during customs control and at the written request of any interested party accompanied by proof of right, retain any goods which that party deems to be infringing. (2) The customs department shall immediately notify the Prosecutor of the Republic, the requester and the importer that the goods have been detained. (3) Such detention at customs shall be automatically lifted if, within 10 working days following detention of the goods, the requester fails to justify to the customs authorities: (a) why the precautionary measures were taken or (b) that civil or criminal proceedings have been instituted before the competent national judge and the required guarantees, if any, have been provided to cover his potential liability ... (4) The requester may obtain the names and addresses of the sender, importer and consignee ... (5) After expiry of the 10 days ... the owner, importer or consignee of the goods may, on deposit of a bond, file for a stay of the decision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Customs can detain suspected infringing goods on request; requester must justify/demonstrate proceedings within 10 working days or detention lifted; parties can obtain shipment data and seek stay on bond.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ex-officio customs action and liability
rubrics_metrics.description: Customs authorities may, ex officio, withhold suspected goods when they have presumptive evidence that the goods are infringing. These authorities may, at any time, request the rightholder to provide any information that may assist them ... The rightholder, the importer or exporter shall be immediately informed of the detention. The customs authorities shall be liable in the event of unjustified detention unless they acted in good faith.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Customs may act on their own initiative but bear liability for unjustified detentions unless in good faith; rightholders must be informed and may be asked for assistance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Retroactive effect (application to pre-existing works)
rubrics_metrics.description: The provisions of this Annex shall also apply to works that were created, to performances that took place or were fixed ... prior to the date of entry into force of this Annex, on condition that such works ... have not yet fallen into the public domain by reason of the expiry of the term of protection which they enjoyed under Article VII of the Bangui Agreement ... or under the legislation of their country of origin.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Annex can apply retroactively to pre-existing protected works that are not yet in the public domain under prior rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Final provisions (repeal and continuity of prior acts/contracts)
rubrics_metrics.description: (1) Part I of Annex VII of the Bangui Agreement ... relating to copyright and neighboring rights, is hereby repealed. (2) The acts and contracts concluded prior to the entry into force of this Annex shall remain in force.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Repeals prior Annex provisions but preserves validity of pre-existing acts and contracts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unfair competition — definitions and general principle
rubrics_metrics.description: Definitions: 'weakening of the image or reputation' means lessening the distinctive character or advertising value of a trademark, trade name, external appearance or get-up of products or services, or of a famous person or well-known fictional character; 'industrial or commercial activities' include liberal professions; 'external appearance' means packaging, shape, color or other non-functional characteristics; 'trademarks' means marks relating to products/services; 'practice' includes acts and omissions; 'presentation of products or services' means advertising; 'distinctive sign of an enterprise' covers signs, symbols, emblems, logos, slogans, etc. Apart from acts in Articles 2-6, an act of unfair competition shall be any act or practice which ... is contrary to honest practice. Any person who has suffered damage may institute proceedings ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establishes vocabulary and baseline: unfair competition covers dishonest commercial/industrial acts that damage enterprise identity or reputation; victims may seek injunctive and civil remedies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confusion with another's enterprise or activities (unfair competition)
rubrics_metrics.description: Any act or practice which ... generates or is likely to generate confusion with the enterprise or activities of another person, in particular with the products or services proposed by such enterprise, shall constitute an act of unfair competition. Confusion may concern, in particular: (a) trademark; (b) trade name; (c) distinctive sign other than trademark; (d) external appearance of a product; (e) the get-up of products or services; and (f) a famous person or well-known fictional character.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Confusion-based acts across marks, product appearance, get-up or famous person appropriation are expressly unfair competition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acts damaging to another's image or reputation (unfair competition)
rubrics_metrics.description: Any act or practice which ... damages or is liable to damage the image or reputation of another’s enterprise, whether the act or the practice generates confusion or not, shall constitute an act of unfair competition. Damage may result, in particular, from a weakening of the image or reputation attaching to: (a) a trademark; (b) a trade name; (c) the distinctive sign of an enterprise; (d) the external appearance of a product; (e) the get-up of products or services; and (f) a famous person or well-known fictional character.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Independent of confusion, acts harming reputation/image of enterprise/material signs are actionable as unfair competition.
